cases.question: How long does a password reset link stay valid before it expires?
cases.answer: Password reset links are valid for 30 minutes before they expire. [source: kb-account-001::section_aware::6]

cases.question: When two devices edit the same file before syncing, what happens to the older version?
cases.answer: When the same file is edited on two devices before either change can upload, the app creates a **conflicted‑copy** file for the older version, preserving it locally while the newer edit is synced. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::2]

cases.question: What is the maximum size allowed for a single file upload?
cases.answer: The application enforces a 2 GB limit for a single‑file upload — files larger than 2 GB must be compressed or split before uploading [ source: kb-errors-006::section_aware::3 ].

cases.question: Can someone with the Commenter role edit the actual content of a document?
cases.answer: No. Commenters can add comments but cannot edit the document’s content. [source: kb-share-003::section_aware::6]

cases.question: If I turn off email notifications for every individual event, does that also stop the weekly digest email?
cases.answer: No. Email notifications for individual events (comments, shares, mentions, storage warnings) are controlled by their own toggles, while the weekly‑digest email has a separate “Weekly Digest” toggle. Turning off all the individual email‑event toggles does not automatically disable the digest—you would need to turn off the weekly‑digest toggle itself. [source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::1] [source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4]

cases.question: How do I stop getting notifications?
cases.answer:
To stop receiving notifications, adjust the settings in the app:

1. **Turn off the notification types you don’t want** – open **Settings → Notifications** and toggle off the events you don’t need (email, push, in‑app, etc.)【source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4】.  
2. **Disable push notifications completely** – in the same Notifications page, turn off the **Push** toggle (push is enabled for all events by default)【source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::7】.  
3. **Mute specific folders** – right‑click a folder and choose **Mute notifications** to stop alerts from that folder【source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4】.  
4. **Turn off the weekly digest** – go to **Settings → Notifications → Weekly Digest** and switch the toggle off if you no longer want the summary email【source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4】.  

After making these changes, the app will stop sending the selected notifications. If you still see alerts after these steps, you may need to verify that the folder isn’t unintentionally muted or that the email address isn’t still subscribed in the admin panel.

cases.question: My account keeps disconnecting whenever I try to move a lot of files
cases.answer:
Here are the most common reasons your sync drops when you move a lot of files and what to do about each one:

1. **Large upload queue** – When many files are queued (over 50 items) the client can become unstable. Open the **Sync Queue** and, if it’s long, pause sync, then resume to reset the queue. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3]

2. **Network instability** – High latency or packet loss often causes “connection blocked” messages. Run a speed test and make sure latency is <150 ms with no loss; use a wired Ethernet connection for big batches. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3]

3. **Firewall/port issues after a network change** – After switching Wi‑Fi or VPN, the client may be blocked. Verify that outbound HTTPS (port 443) is allowed and that your firewall permits `*.filesync.example`. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3]

4. **Files larger than 2 GB** – The app enforces a single‑file size limit. Compress files larger than 2 GB into a zip (or split them) before moving them. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3]

5. **Accidentally excluded folders** – If a folder was set to “Don’t sync on this device,” moving files from it will stop syncing. Re‑enable “Sync on this device” for the folder. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3]

These steps address the typical root causes (large queue, unstable network, firewall blocks, oversized files, or folder exclusion) that lead to frequent disconnects when moving many files. [source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::2]

cases.question: I want to make sure only my team can see a folder, not the whole company — how?
cases.answer:
To keep the folder visible only to your team, turn off public link sharing and invite just your teammates:

1. **Disable “anyone with the link”** – In the admin console go to **Settings → Sharing → Link Sharing** and make sure the option is turned off. When this is disabled, users must add specific email addresses instead of using a public link【source: kb-share-003::section_aware::3】.  
2. **Invite your team members** – Open the folder’s **Sharing Settings** and add the email addresses of the team members who should have access.  
3. **Use the “Restrict sharing to workspace”** option for the folder (especially for large folders) so it can’t be shared outside the workspace unintentionally【source: kb-share-003::section_aware::9】.  

After these steps, only the invited teammates will be able to see the folder, and the rest of the company won’t have access.

cases.question: How do I stop getting notifications?
cases.answer:
To stop receiving notifications, follow these steps:

1. **Turn off the notification toggles you don’t want** – open **Settings → Notifications** and disable the switches for each event type you wish to stop receiving [ source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4 ].  

2. **Disable push notifications entirely** – in the same Settings page, turn off the **Push** toggle (push notifications are currently enabled for all events) [ source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::7 ].  

3. **Mute any folders that are still sending alerts** – right‑click the folder, choose **Mute notifications**, and confirm the folder isn’t unintentionally muted [ source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4 ].  

4. **Turn off the weekly digest email** – go to **Settings → Notifications → Weekly Digest** and toggle it off [ source: kb-notify-005::section_aware::4 ].  

After applying these changes, the user will no longer receive the corresponding in‑app, push, or email notifications. If alerts still appear, double‑check that the folder mute and weekly‑digest settings are correctly saved.

cases.question: I keep getting logged out and my files won't upload, what's going on?
cases.answer:
You’re likely dealing with two related problems:

* **Sign‑out issues** – Unexpected sign‑out errors and session‑expiration problems are common symptoms that cause a user to be logged out even after a successful login [ source: kb-account-001::section_aware::1 ].

* **Sync/upload failures** – Files can stay “sync pending” or fail to upload when the network is unstable, the sync queue is large, or the file exceeds size limits [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::1 ]; you can also see upload failures after switching networks or when corporate firewalls block outbound HTTPS [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3 ].

**What to try**

1. **Check active sessions** – Go to **Settings → Security → Active Sessions** to confirm no other device is revoking your token [ source: kb-account-001::section_aware::6 ].
2. **Verify sync service status** – Open the tray icon → **Sync Dashboard** for any outage notices [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3 ].
3. **Inspect the sync queue** – If it exceeds 50 items, pause sync, then resume to reset the queue [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3 ].
4. **Test network stability** – Run a speed test; aim for latency < 150 ms, no packet loss, and ensure outbound HTTPS (port 443) is allowed [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3 ].
5. **Handle large files** – For files > 2 GB, compress or split them before uploading [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3 ].
6. **After a network change** – Click the **Sync** icon and select **Resume**; if you see “connection blocked,” verify firewall rules for `*.filesync.example` [ source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3 ].

If the problem persists after these steps, it may require further investigation by support.

cases.question: My account keeps disconnecting whenever I try to move a lot of files
cases.answer:
It sounds like the disconnects are being caused by the sync client being overloaded while it tries to process a large batch of moves.

**What to try**

1. **Check the upload queue** – Open **Sync Queue** and see if it has more than 50 items. If it does, pause the sync, then resume it to reset the queue【source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3】.  
2. **Verify your network** – Run a speed test and make sure latency is under 150 ms with no packet loss. A wired Ethernet connection helps with big transfers【source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3】.  
3. **Handle files larger than 2 GB** – The client enforces a 2 GB single‑file limit. Compress or split any oversized files before moving them【source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3】.  
4. **Check firewall/VPN settings** – After a network change (e.g., switching Wi‑Fi or connecting to a corporate VPN) the badge may show **“connection blocked.”** Make sure outbound HTTPS (port 443) is allowed and that `*.filesync.example` is whitelisted【source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3】.  
5. **Confirm folder sync is enabled** – Right‑click the folder, choose **Sync Settings**, and verify **“Sync on this device”** is turned on. Re‑enable it if it was accidentally excluded【source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::3】.  

These steps address the common root causes for “sync pending” or disconnects when moving many files, such as a large upload queue, unstable network, or firewall blocks【source: kb-sync-002::section_aware::2】. If the problem persists after trying the above, let us know the exact error message or any error codes you see.

cases.question: I want to make sure only my team can see a folder, not the whole company — how?
cases.answer:
To keep the folder visible only to your team, change its sharing settings so it isn’t exposed with a public link:

1. Open the folder’s **Sharing Settings**.  
2. Turn off “anyone with the link” (Admins can disable this globally under **Settings → Sharing → Link Sharing**) and instead **invite only the email addresses of your team members** with the appropriate role [ source: kb-share-003::section_aware::3 ].  
3. For large folders, enable the **“Restrict sharing to workspace”** option, which limits visibility to members of your workspace and prevents accidental company‑wide exposure [ source: kb-share-003::section_aware::9 ].  

After these steps, only the invited team members will be able to access the folder.
